title: Any Claude Code skills you’d recommend for building a 3D game from scratch?
author: owen800q
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I’m planning to build a 3D game from scratch with AI assistance. I currently have **both Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions**, and I also plan to use **GPT Image 2.5 to design assets and create concept art**.

Are there any **Claude Code skills, plugins, MCP servers, or workflows** you’d recommend for this?

I haven’t picked an engine yet, so I’m open to Unity, Unreal, Godot, or other suggestions. I’m mainly looking for help with:

* Project setup and code organization
* Player movement, cameras, physics, and gameplay mechanics
* Debugging and testing
* Designing assets and bringing them into the game engine
* Keeping the project maintainable as it grows

If you’ve used a similar setup, how would you split tasks between Claude Code, ChatGPT, and image generation? I’d also love advice on turning AI-generated concept art into usable 3D assets—I know generating an image isn’t the same as creating a game-ready model.

My goal is a **small, playable prototype**, not a huge game. Any recommended skills, repos, tutorials, or examples would be appreciated. Thanks!

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body: Just a heads up but the Unity MCP is deprecated, it’s recommended to use the Unity CLI binary and the Unity Pipeline package instead of that to drive the Unity Editor from the terminal.

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: Can you link me any documentation on that? I have been using the Unity MCP with success for months included extensively today. Always open to improving my workflow though.

replies.author: cckynv
replies.body:
https://unity.com/resources/unity-pipeline-cli-technical-walkthrough

Sure thing, this goes over all of its capabilities as well as how to set it up.

From my personal experience using both, it consumes less tokens than using the MCP.

comments.author: Tron_bonneLoFi
comments.body:
Do you have any advices for beginners on what they should study to avoid most of the common mistakes? 

I want to do something like you but I have no idea where to start. I never even used Claude.

replies.author: Careless_Road8873
replies.body:
Happy to help. Here’s where I’d start:

1. **Learn just enough of the engine to read it.** Do Godot’s own “Your first 2D game” tutorial (an afternoon). You won’t write the code later, but you’ll know what a scene, a node and a script are, so you can understand what the AI tells you.
2. **Start Claude on something tiny.** One screen, one mechanic (a character that moves and picks up coins). Ask it to explain each change in plain words. You’re learning how to describe what you want, and that’s the real skill.
3. **From day one:** a handover file in the project, and small tests for every mechanic. Ask Claude to set both up. It feels like overkill early, but it’s what lets the project grow without falling apart.
4. **Common beginner mistakes:** Decide, then let it type.
   * starting with the dream game
   * asking for ten things in one message
   * accepting changes without playing them
   * letting the AI make design decisions for you
5. **Use git (or at least backups) before every big change,** so a bad session costs you nothing.

If you’d like, I can walk you through the whole setup in one session over Discord: the engine, Claude, the handover file and tests, with a first mechanic working by the end. Just DM me.

replies.author: Patera-Milenko
replies.body:
All great advice man. I've learnt every one of these the hard way lol. The other thing I've got it doing is focusing on one task at a time then do the hand off. It's slower but it's helped me. 

I'm not an authority by any means though so I'm way open to critiques lol.

Legit though you're advice is really good. 

I've also added a lessons feature per session. So it tracks what failed and why, how it got fixed and gives us options to prevent making the same mistake in the future (in theory lol).

It's been working so far though, knock on wood lol

replies.author: Careless_Road8873
replies.body: Ha, same, every one of those cost me a bad evening first. The lessons log is a great idea, I do something similar in the handover file: what broke, why, and the rule so it doesn't happen again. One task per session has saved me more than anything else too. Good luck with your project!

replies.author: Patera-Milenko
replies.body:
Dude it's legit nice to see you say this, share this and not be like man your setup is totally messed lol Makes me feel like I'm making some head way lol

A really fun side project that just eats up tokens but is helping me is this. So I'm using CC via cli to run universal modder to mod Abiotic Factor, a game I dearly love. 

I setup a Prof agent that knows the "proper" way to code things. A Dev agent that knows the hacks and shortcuts that work and don't break code (hopefully) and a Tutor agent that creates lessons. Let's me try things and corrects and shows me the "proper" way. 

There is probably a way better way forward here but it's helping me understand things so far I think lol

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: For a small 3D prototype I'd go Godot or plain Three.js, since scenes and scripts are text files Claude can read and edit directly. The biggest win is keeping a short design doc and TODO file in the repo that it rereads every session, and committing after each working step so you can roll back when it breaks something. Greybox everything with primitives first and only swap in generated models once the core loop is actually fun.

comments.author: Abject-Constant784
comments.body:
Some MCP servers if you need, and just scratch Claude.

If you want to design a really good game, Claude Code Game Studios GitHub repo has alot of great skills and tools, but it's extremely in-depth... You basically need a full game design document for the CCGS to work, and it will build a GDD with you if you want even... I don't recommend using it on your first project.

comments.author: Otherwise-Syrup-5589
comments.body:
Use claude superpowers plugin to be forced to always spec and plan any feature. It also forces test driven development and code reviews. 
Start small with placeholder graphics first. E.g. movements and basic gameplay first.
Let claude build you a test laboratory early on where you can balance everything by playtesting. E.g. load lvl X with enemies Y with stats Z. 
Let claude build you a paralleized headless bot to autonomously let claude playtest and balance your game without opening the Game. Let claude optimize this to e.g. playtest 200 runs in no time. 
Iterate on that...

comments.author: Big_Insurance_2509
comments.body: Get Claude to build skills after a successful session. Set up a session review mod and skill hygiene mod. Every successful prop, render etc etc becomes a script or a skill. Keep in mind that while you are building your first game you will be building an ai pipeline that is building its first game.
